# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
KEYPAD 1:[ᘔ] 2:[꩜] 3:[ꓭ] 4:[ꓕ] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 👇 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

I can see the bomb but cannot operate it. The current visible state is display `0`, yellow light, four keypad glyphs, and three wires. The earlier gestures from Mute have no established meaning, so I will define a numbered gesture code for Mute to use next round. I will also give Blind the bomb layout and tell them to wait for the manual instructions relayed through me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The earlier gesture strings are not yet interpretable. Use the gesture alphabet by position, counting from the first symbol shown in the alphabet. Positions 1 through 10 mean digits zero through nine. Position 23 is a word separator. Position 11 means keypad, 12 wire, 13 press, 14 cut, 15 turn, 16 hold, 17 display, 18 light, 19 finish, 20 cancel, 21 yes, 22 no. Positions 24 red, 25 yellow, 26 green, 27 blue, 28 white, 29 black. Send the manual instruction as gesture-position tokens, using position 23 between words. Send one instruction at a time next round.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible bomb state: display reads 0. Indicator light is yellow. Keypad keys are numbered 1 through 4; their printed glyphs are, respectively, an angular reversed-Z-like glyph, a ring with a central mark, a reversed-B-like glyph, and an upside-down-T-like glyph. Wires 1 through 3 are red, yellow, and green. Do not act yet; Mute will provide manual instructions through me using a gesture code, and I will relay them in speech.")
wait()
```

The new gesture 🫱 is the thirteenth symbol in the agreed numbering, meaning “press.” It is only a partial instruction and gives no target, so Blind must not act. I will ask Mute to send the complete manual instruction, including the target and any required value.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received position 13, meaning press, but the instruction is incomplete. Send the full instruction, including what to press and any required digit or condition. Use position 23 between words.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has sent only the partial instruction PRESS. Do not act. I am requesting the complete target and any required value.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 👋 👈 👋 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

The Mute’s message follows the structure “press / keypad / [one],” using the agreed meanings for positions 13 and 11. I previously described positions 1–10 as digits zero through nine, but a keypad target must instead be identified by its key number; in this context the final 👍 most plausibly means key 1. I will not tell Blind to press until Mute confirms that interpretation. Blind’s 🫵 has no assigned meaning.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I decode your message as PRESS KEYPAD 1, but please confirm by repeating the same message and then adding YES. The final thumbs-up must mean key 1 here, not digit 0.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest message appears to instruct PRESS KEYPAD 1, but this is not yet confirmed. Do not act. I am requesting confirmation.")
wait()
```

The complete gesture sequence decodes under the agreed code as “PRESS KEYPAD 0 YES”: 🫱 = press, 👋 = separator, 👈 = keypad, 👋 = separator, 👍 = digit 0, 👋 = separator, ✊ = yes. However, the bomb has only keypad keys 1–4, so this cannot safely authorize an action. I will ask Mute to correct or clarify the target and keep Blind from acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I decode the complete message as PRESS KEYPAD 0 YES, but the bomb has only keys 1 through 4. Please resend the exact valid keypad key number, using the agreed code.")
speak(to="blind", text="The received instruction decodes as PRESS KEYPAD 0, which is invalid because the bomb shows only keys 1 through 4. Do not act; I have requested clarification.")
wait()
```

Mute has repeated the same confirmed instruction: press the keypad with value `0` and confirm. The `0` is the required one-digit entry, not a physical key number; Blind must use the physical key whose manual-defined function enters zero. I will ask Mute to identify that physical key using the available key numbers, and I will not authorize a guess.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your instruction is PRESS KEYPAD 0 YES. Which physical key, numbered 1 through 4, enters digit 0? Send the key number after the same instruction, using our digit-position code.")
speak(to="blind", text="The confirmed instruction requires entering digit 0 on the keypad and then confirming. I am asking Mute which physical key numbered 1 through 4 produces digit 0. Do not press yet.")

```

speak(to="blind", text="Mute has repeated digit 0, not the physical key number. Do not press anything; I have requested a key number from 1 through 4.")

The keypad has opened, and its entry is now shown as `5`, so the previous relay resulted in an accepted action. Mute’s new 👍 again conveys digit `0`, but without separators it is not enough to determine the next manual step. I will relay the successful state and request the next complete instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The keypad opened after the previous action. The display now shows entered digit 5. Do not take another action until the next manual instruction is relayed.")
speak(to="mute", text="The keypad opened successfully. Please send the next complete manual instruction, with gesture separators between words and all required targets or values.")
wait()
```
